paper.title: Synthetic HAR-RV intake control fixture
paper.bibliography: ATHENA Test Laboratory (2026). Synthetic HAR-RV intake control fixture. Synthetic fixture; not an academic source.

research_card.summary: Synthetic description of volatility persistence across daily, weekly, and monthly components.
research_card.research_question: Can a reproducible HAR-RV proxy improve volatility-state measurement across an approved universe?
research_card.method: Control fixture only; no empirical market test is claimed.
findings: The fixture declares a testable multi-horizon volatility-persistence mechanism.
limitations: The source is synthetic and cannot establish empirical validity.
No licensed market data, out-of-sample evidence, or Pine parity exists.
assumptions: Realised-volatility inputs will be defined before implementation.
No coefficient is accepted before controlled estimation and validation.
counter_evidence: A simple persistence model may fail during structural breaks or discontinuous volatility shocks.

claims.statement: Volatility persistence may contain separable daily, weekly, and monthly components.

hypotheses.claim: A multi-horizon realised-volatility proxy will outperform a single-horizon persistence baseline on unseen data.
hypotheses.mechanism: Daily shocks and slower weekly and monthly persistence contribute distinct forecast information.
hypotheses.falsification: Reject if the proxy fails the approved walk-forward, cross-market, sensitivity, or robustness gates.

formulas.applicability: Research specification only; empirical and Pine-compatible definitions remain unapproved.
assumptions: Input windows, annualisation, sampling, and estimator definitions will be versioned.
